तथास्य नाधिक्यमपैति किंचिदनादियोगेन भवन्ति पुंसः ॥ २० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
doṣo mahān atra vibhedayoge hy anādiyogena bhavanti nityāḥ |
tathāsya nādhikyam apaiti kiṃcid anādiyogena bhavanti puṃsaḥ || 20 ||

lines.iast: doṣo mahān atra vibhedayoge hy anādiyogena bhavanti nityāḥ
lines.deva: दोषो महानत्र विभेदयोगे ह्यनादियोगेन भवन्ति नित्याः

lines.iast: tathāsya nādhikyam apaiti kiṃcid anādiyogena bhavanti puṃsaḥ

padaccheda.iast: doṣaḥ mahān atra vibheda-yoge hi anādi-yogena bhavanti nityāḥ tathā asya na ādhikyam apaiti kiṃcit anādi-yogena bhavanti puṃsaḥ
padaccheda.deva: दोषः महान् अत्र विभेद-योगे हि अनादि-योगेन भवन्ति नित्याः तथा अस्य न आधिक्यम् अपैति किंचित् अनादि-योगेन भवन्ति पुंसः

translations.text: Great is the fault here, in (the view of) difference. (The jīvas and the rest) are eternal by the beginningless union (with māyā); so nothing of his pre-eminence departs at all. By the beginningless union (with māyā) the persons (the jīvas, many) come to be.

notes: puṃsaḥ: Śaṅkara takes the word first as nominative plural (pumāṃsaḥ, the jīvas), then, second, as genitive singular: by union with the beginningless māyā of the Puruṣa, the full Supreme Self, (the many) come to be.

Śaṅkara: the objector's thought is this: from seeing a difference of director and directed, impossible in one changeless being, there must be difference. If plurality is granted to Brahman itself, then in this vibhedayoga, Brahman's being many, the fault is great: the non-dualists would be speakers of untruth and outside the Veda, the non-dual supreme truth, the heart of the Veda, would be sublated; and being turned into many forms, Brahman would be impermanent and the like, against ‘not gross …’ (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.8.8). If instead it is said that not Brahman's plurality but a difference between the jīva and the Supreme is held, there too the fault is great: destruction follows (Taittirīya 2.7: when he makes the least difference in it, fear comes to him; Kaṭha 2.1.10: from death to death goes he who sees difference here; Bṛhadāraṇyaka 1.4.10: he who worships another deity, thinking ‘he is one, I another’, does not know, he is like a beast; Chāndogya 7.25.2: those who know otherwise have perishable worlds; Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.4.6). Or, with difference between the jīva and the Supreme, one speaks against ‘that thou art’, ‘I am Brahman’, ‘this Self is Brahman’, ‘the Self within all’, ‘this is your Self, the inner controller, the deathless’, ‘all this is that Self’, ‘I am you, O deity, you are I’, ‘this great unborn Self … is Brahman, the fearless’, and the like in śruti, smṛti, itihāsa and purāṇa: the great fault of being outside the Veda.

Śaṅkara: how then, on your view, do the dealings of jīva, Lord and the rest come about, and how are they eternal? ‘By the beginningless union they are eternal’: the beginningless is māyā, called ignorance (Gītā 13.19: know Prakṛti and Puruṣa both to be beginningless; a verse: she is the one womb of the world, the self of all, ruler of all, the beginningless power of Maheśvara). By union with that beginningless māyā the jīvas and the rest are eternal: the Supreme Self, though without a second, can well have many forms by māyā. The śruti tells of the one having many forms by māyā: ‘he became the counterpart of every form’, ‘Indra by his māyās goes in many forms’ (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.5.19), ‘the one god hidden in all beings’ (Śvetāśvatara 6.11), ‘the sages call the one being by many names’ (Ṛgveda 1.164.46), ‘unborn, he is born in many ways’, and more; so the Mokṣadharma (the one self of beings is seen as one and many, like the moon in water), Yājñavalkya (as the one space is separate in pots, so the one Self is many, like the sun in vessels of water), the Kāvaṣeya-gītā (Brahman in all bodies, within and without, like space in jars) and the Supreme Lord (the eternal Self, all-pervading, changeless, one, is divided by the power that is māyā).

Śaṅkara: since the one has many forms by māyā alone, that same Supreme Lord, the self as cause, directs the self as effect, the jīva, by māyā, according to the effort the jīva has made; in truth he neither transmigrates nor makes another transmigrate (the Kāvaṣeya-gītā: he is not born, does not die, is neither slain nor slayer, neither bound nor binder, neither freed nor freeing; what is other than the Supreme Self is unreal; the Lord: ‘I am the ruler of all, by a nature beyond māyā; this lord neither transmigrates nor makes transmigrate’). Moreover, with a difference caused by māyā granted, the Supreme Self, though standing as effect and cause, loses nothing of his pre-eminence, the pre-eminence of his own nature, for saṃsāra is of the nature of māyā: he stays changeless as before. Therefore by union with beginningless ignorance the persons, the jīvas, come to be many; or, by union with the beginningless māyā of the Puruṣa, the full Supreme Self, they come to be many.

Śaṅkara, the authorities he then quotes: the Anugītā (the Self, standing as ignorance and the guṇas; endowed with the power of ignorance it moves in all births; that delusion is to be abandoned; when the sense of ‘I’ is conquered the Self is accomplished; the devotee, by the grace of the Supreme, with the fire of knowledge, burns up all action and reaches the deathless called Viṣṇu); and Parāśara (the Viṣṇu Purāṇa, at length): knowledge, utterly pure, is the reality, and by error it stands as objects; the unwise see the world, which is knowledge, as objects and wander in a flood of delusion, while the pure-minded see it as knowledge; mountains, seas and earth are the play of consciousness; earth becomes a pot, the pot sherds, the sherds powder, the powder atoms — ‘tell me, what here is a thing?’; there is nothing at any time but knowledge, one, seen as many by minds divided by their own actions; the one All is Acyuta, ‘he is I, he is you, he is all this; give up the delusion of difference’; hearing this the king gave up difference and was freed in that birth; when ignorance, which makes difference, is wholly destroyed, who will make the unreal difference of the self and Brahman?; knowledge alone is the supreme Brahman.

Śaṅkara, on renunciation: Sanatsujāta himself says all this plainly in the Kāvaṣeya-gītā of the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa. The Kāvaṣeyas, told to study the Vedas, marry, sacrifice, beget sons and at the end leave the body by austerity, answer that study and sacrifice serve them nothing, their work being done (‘we offer prāṇa in speech and speech in prāṇa’); he shows the world won by sacrifice to be faulty, impermanent (heaven ends in a fall when merit is spent, like a courtesan's house). The Yajurveda Upaniṣad (the Mahānārāyaṇa), after praising truth and the rest, ranks renunciation (nyāsa) above all, as the means to Brahman, eternal and unsurpassed bliss: ‘not by action, not by offspring or wealth; by renunciation some reached deathlessness … the renouncers, pure in mind, whose meaning is fixed by the knowledge of the Vedānta, by the yoga of renunciation are all freed in the worlds of Brahmā at the end’. So too the Bṛhadāraṇyaka (4.4.22), Vāsudeva (Gītā 4.21, 12.16, 12.17, 14.25, 18.49, 18.66), the Anugītā (knowledge is marked by renunciation; so, putting knowledge first, let the wise man renounce), Vyāsa to Śuka in the Śāntiparvan (a creature is bound by action, freed by knowledge; so the renouncers do no action; let him go forth to the life of the wandering mendicant), Nārada (renouncing all actions, austerity and learning, with a lump of food for support one can wander everywhere; giving up truth and untruth one becomes free of the guṇas), Bṛhaspati (only one restrained, free of passion, gains knowledge), and Brahmā in the Āśvamedhika (the householder, the brahmacārin or the forest-dweller who wishes for liberation should take to the highest way). Hence for both the knower and the seeker of liberation, the renunciation of all action alone is fitting.

Śaṅkara, closing: so far the one Supreme Self's having many forms by union with beginningless māyā has been told; now he says that the Lord's being the cause of the world is also due to the adjunct, māyā.

sanskrit.deva:
यदेतदद्धा भगवान्स नित्यं विकारयोगेन करोति विश्वम् ।
तथा च तच्छक्तिरिति स्म मन्ये तदर्थयोगे च भवन्ति वेदाः ॥ २१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yad etad addhā bhagavān sa nityaṃ vikārayogena karoti viśvam |
tathā ca tacchaktir iti sma manye tadarthayoge ca bhavanti vedāḥ || 21 ||

lines.iast: yad etad addhā bhagavān sa nityaṃ vikārayogena karoti viśvam
lines.deva: यदेतदद्धा भगवान्स नित्यं विकारयोगेन करोति विश्वम्

lines.iast: tathā ca tacchaktir iti sma manye tadarthayoge ca bhavanti vedāḥ
lines.deva: तथा च तच्छक्तिरिति स्म मन्ये तदर्थयोगे च भवन्ति वेदाः

padaccheda.iast: yat etat addhā bhagavān saḥ nityam vikāra-yogena karoti viśvam tathā ca tat-śaktiḥ iti sma manye tat-artha-yoge ca bhavanti vedāḥ
padaccheda.deva: यत् एतत् अद्धा भगवान् सः नित्यम् विकार-योगेन करोति विश्वम् तथा च तत्-शक्तिः इति स्म मन्ये तत्-अर्थ-योगे च भवन्ति वेदाः

translations.text: That the Lord, truly, always makes the universe by union with modification — so it is; and I think it is his power (māyā, that makes it); and for his union with that (māyā) the Vedas are (the proof).

notes: Śaṅkara: that the Lord, real in truth, endowed with lordship and the rest, the Supreme Lord, always makes the universe by union with modification, preceded by seeing (īkṣaṇa) and the rest — all that is so; but it is his power, the power of the Supreme Self, māyā alone, that makes it, not the Supreme Self, who is without before or after: so I think. Causality does not belong to him, consciousness and bliss without a second, by himself, but by his entering into māyā. What proves that he is joined with such a power? ‘In his union with that the Vedas are’: for the existence of māyā, the material cause of the world, the Vedas are the means of knowledge (Ṛgveda: ‘Indra by his māyās goes in many forms’; Śvetāśvatara 4.9: from this the master of māyā creates the universe; 4.10: know the great Lord as the master of māyā; 1.3: the power of the god, hidden by its own guṇas; Gītā 7.14, 4.6, 9.10; and verses: this māyā of yours deludes those who do not know things, by it the fool mounts the knowledge of self on the not-self; hard to cross is this deep māyā of Viṣṇu, by which deluded the mind does not know the Supreme Lord).

Śaṅkara, closing: so far, by ‘I call heedlessness death’ and what follows, the nature of death, its standing as its effects and the many evils it causes have been shown; asked how it is destroyed, he showed that fearlessness comes from knowledge of the Self alone (verse 16); and the two incidental objections (verses 17 and 19) have been answered. Now Dhṛtarāṣṭra speaks, to learn the nature of action.
The edition: the transcript marks tacchaktir iti as doubtful in the print; the reading is kept.

sanskrit.deva:
यस्माद्धर्मानाचरन्तीह केचित्तथाधर्मान्केचिदिहाचरन्ति ।
धर्मः पापेन प्रतिहन्यते वा उताहो धर्मः प्रतिहन्ति पापम् ॥ २२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yasmād dharmān ācarantīha kecit tathādharmān kecid ihācaranti |
dharmaḥ pāpena pratihanyate vā utāho dharmaḥ pratihanti pāpam || 22 ||

lines.iast: yasmād dharmān ācarantīha kecit tathādharmān kecid ihācaranti
dharmaḥ pāpena pratihanyate vā utāho dharmaḥ pratihanti pāpam
lines.deva: धर्मः पापेन प्रतिहन्यते वा उताहो धर्मः प्रतिहन्ति पापम्

padaccheda.iast: yasmāt dharmān ācaranti iha kecit tathā adharmān kecit iha ācaranti dharmaḥ pāpena pratihanyate vā utāho dharmaḥ pratihanti pāpam
padaccheda.deva: यस्मात् धर्मान् आचरन्ति इह केचित् तथा अधर्मान् केचित् इह आचरन्ति धर्मः पापेन प्रतिहन्यते वा उताहो धर्मः प्रतिहन्ति पापम्

translations.text: Since some here practise dharmas, and likewise some here practise adharmas: is dharma struck down by sin, or else does dharma strike down sin?

notes: Śaṅkara: some in this world practise dharmas, the agnihotra and the rest, and likewise some practise adharmas. Is their dharma struck down by sin, or does dharma strike down sin? Or, the two being equal in strength, is each destroyed by the other?
Śaṅkara, introducing the answer: for the ignorant both are only experienced, neither destroys the other; for the knower both are destroyed by the fire of knowledge.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्मिन्स्थितो वाप्युभयं हि नित्यं ज्ञानेन विद्वान्प्रतिहन्ति सिद्धम् ।
अथान्यथा पुण्यमुपैति देही तथागतं पापमुपैति सिद्धम् ॥ २३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmin sthito vāpy ubhayaṃ hi nityaṃ jñānena vidvān pratihanti siddham |
athānyathā puṇyam upaiti dehī tathāgataṃ pāpam upaiti siddham || 23 ||

lines.iast: tasmin sthito vāpy ubhayaṃ hi nityaṃ jñānena vidvān pratihanti siddham
lines.deva: तस्मिन्स्थितो वाप्युभयं हि नित्यं ज्ञानेन विद्वान्प्रतिहन्ति सिद्धम्

lines.iast: athānyathā puṇyam upaiti dehī tathāgataṃ pāpam upaiti siddham
lines.deva: अथान्यथा पुण्यमुपैति देही तथागतं पापमुपैति सिद्धम्

padaccheda.iast: tasmin sthitaḥ vā api ubhayam hi nityam jñānena vidvān pratihanti siddham atha anyathā puṇyam upaiti dehī tathā-gatam pāpam upaiti siddham
padaccheda.deva: तस्मिन् स्थितः वा अपि उभयम् हि नित्यम् ज्ञानेन विद्वान् प्रतिहन्ति सिद्धम् अथ अन्यथा पुण्यम् उपैति देही तथा-गतम् पापम् उपैति सिद्धम्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.
past active participle m. nom. sg.
past passive participle n. nom. sg.
past passive participle n. acc. sg.
past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: Even standing in it (action), the knower always strikes down both by knowledge: that is established. But otherwise, the embodied one gains merit, and gains sin that comes likewise (and enjoys their fruit): that (too) is established.

notes: Śaṅkara: tasmin: in action, of merit and demerit; even standing in it, even while doing it, the knower always, without fail, strikes down, destroys, both kinds of action, of merit and of demerit, by knowledge. How is this known? It is established, well known, in śruti, smṛti, itihāsa and purāṇa: ‘the knot of the heart is cut’ (Muṇḍaka 2.2.8); ‘as water does not cling to a lotus leaf, so sinful action does not cling to one who knows thus’ (Chāndogya 4.14.3); ‘as the tuft of a reed laid in fire is burnt up, so are all his sins burnt up’ (Chāndogya 5.24.3); ‘then the knower, shaking off merit and sin, stainless, reaches the highest sameness’ (Muṇḍaka 3.1.3); ‘shaking off sin as a horse its hairs’ (Chāndogya 8.13.1); ‘as kindled fire turns fuel to ashes, Arjuna’ (Gītā 4.37). But otherwise, if without knowledge, the embodied one gains merit and likewise sin, and enjoys their fruit. This too is established in śruti, smṛti and the rest: Muṇḍaka 1.2.10 (thinking sacrifice and works of merit the best, the deluded know no other good; having enjoyed on the back of heaven, they enter this world again); ‘joyless are those worlds, covered by blind darkness; to them, after death, go those who slay the self’; and Vāsudeva (Gītā 9.20–21).
Śaṅkara, introducing the next verse: for the ignorant, are both only experienced, or does one destroy the other?

sanskrit.deva:
गत्वोभयं कर्मणा भुज्यतेऽस्थिरं शुभस्य पापस्य स चापि कर्मणा ।
धर्मेण पापं प्रणुदतीह विद्वान्धर्मो बलीयानिति तस्य विद्धि ॥ २४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
gatvobhayaṃ karmaṇā bhujyate 'sthiraṃ śubhasya pāpasya sa cāpi karmaṇā |
dharmeṇa pāpaṃ praṇudatīha vidvān dharmo balīyān iti tasya viddhi || 24 ||

lines.iast: gatvobhayaṃ karmaṇā bhujyate 'sthiraṃ śubhasya pāpasya sa cāpi karmaṇā
lines.deva: गत्वोभयं कर्मणा भुज्यतेऽस्थिरं शुभस्य पापस्य स चापि कर्मणा

lines.iast: dharmeṇa pāpaṃ praṇudatīha vidvān dharmo balīyān iti tasya viddhi
lines.deva: धर्मेण पापं प्रणुदतीह विद्वान्धर्मो बलीयानिति तस्य विद्धि

padaccheda.iast: gatvā ubhayam karmaṇā bhujyate asthiram śubhasya pāpasya saḥ ca api karmaṇā dharmeṇa pāpam praṇudati iha vidvān dharmaḥ balīyān iti tasya viddhi
padaccheda.deva: गत्वा उभयम् कर्मणा भुज्यते अस्थिरम् शुभस्य पापस्य सः च अपि कर्मणा धर्मेण पापम् प्रणुदति इह विद्वान् धर्मः बलीयान् इति तस्य विद्धि

grammar.en: past active participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Having gone (to the other world), both (fruits), unstable, are enjoyed through the action of good and of evil. And he too, the knower, by action, by dharma, drives away sin here: know that for him dharma is the stronger.

notes: Śaṅkara: having gone, having reached the other world, both, the fruit won by merit and by demerit, unstable, are enjoyed through action of merit and demerit (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.8.10: who, not knowing this imperishable, offers in this world …; Chāndogya 7.25.2: those who know otherwise have perishable worlds). And he too, the knower, by action, by dharma, drives away, destroys, sin here in this world: the knower who will be described, who knows the right use (of action) and performs action for the Lord. So he says below (adhyāya 2): for that are austerity and sacrifice taught; by them the knower gains merit; by merit destroying sin he is then born lit by knowledge; by knowledge the knower reaches the Self; otherwise, longing for the fruit of heaven, he takes all he did here, enjoys it there and comes again to the path; and (verse 26) those who have no rivalry in dharma, for them it is the means to knowledge. For the knower who so knows the right use and performs action for the Lord, know that dharma is stronger than sin; not for the man of mere rites: for him both are only experienced, neither destroys the other.
Śaṅkara, introducing verses 25 and 26: for whom then is (action) the means to heaven and the rest, and for whom the means to knowledge through the purifying of the mind? He answers in two verses.
The edition: the transcript marks tasya as doubtful in the print (‘t’ and ‘n’ look alike in the bold type); the reading is kept.

sanskrit.deva:
येषां धर्मेषु विस्पर्धा बले बलवतामिव ।
ते ब्राह्मणा इतः प्रेत्य स्वर्गे यान्ति प्रकाशताम् ॥ २५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yeṣāṃ dharmeṣu vispardhā bale balavatām iva |
te brāhmaṇā itaḥ pretya svarge yānti prakāśatām || 25 ||

lines.iast: yeṣāṃ dharmeṣu vispardhā bale balavatām iva
te brāhmaṇā itaḥ pretya svarge yānti prakāśatām
lines.deva: ते ब्राह्मणा इतः प्रेत्य स्वर्गे यान्ति प्रकाशताम्

padaccheda.iast: yeṣām dharmeṣu vispardhā bale balavatām iva te brāhmaṇāḥ itaḥ pretya svarge yānti prakāśatām
padaccheda.deva: येषाम् धर्मेषु विस्पर्धा बले बलवताम् इव ते ब्राह्मणाः इतः प्रेत्य स्वर्गे यान्ति प्रकाशताम्

translations.text: Those who have rivalry in dharmas, like the strong in strength — those brāhmaṇas, departing from here, go to brightness in heaven.

notes: Śaṅkara comments on verses 25 and 26 together.

Śaṅkara: those given to objects, hearing of the enjoyment of Urvaśī and the like in the dwelling of heaven, feel rivalry, contention, over the dharmas that are its means, the Jyotiṣṭoma and the rest: ‘doing a better dharma than this man, may I be happier than he’. ‘Like the strong in strength’: as a strong king, seeing a strong king, contends, ‘gaining more strength than he and conquering him, may I be happier than he’. Those brāhmaṇas, entitled to sacrifice and attached to its fruit, departing from here by the path of smoke and the rest, reach brightness in heaven, in the form of stars and the like (Chāndogya 5.10.3–5: those who worship sacrifice, works of merit and gifts go to smoke … this is King Soma, the food of the gods; having stayed there until it is spent, they return by the same way).
The edition: the transcript notes that prakāśatām reads like prakāśanām in the scan; the bhāṣya has prakāśatām.

sanskrit.deva:
येषां धर्मे न च स्पर्धा तेषां तज्ज्ञानसाधनम् ।
ते ब्राह्मणा इतो मुक्ताः स्वर्गं यान्ति त्रिविष्टपम् ॥ २६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yeṣāṃ dharme na ca spardhā teṣāṃ tajjñānasādhanam |
te brāhmaṇā ito muktāḥ svargaṃ yānti triviṣṭapam || 26 ||

lines.iast: yeṣāṃ dharme na ca spardhā teṣāṃ tajjñānasādhanam
lines.deva: येषां धर्मे न च स्पर्धा तेषां तज्ज्ञानसाधनम्

lines.iast: te brāhmaṇā ito muktāḥ svargaṃ yānti triviṣṭapam
lines.deva: ते ब्राह्मणा इतो मुक्ताः स्वर्गं यान्ति त्रिविष्टपम्

padaccheda.iast: yeṣām dharme na ca spardhā teṣām tat jñāna-sādhanam te brāhmaṇāḥ itaḥ muktāḥ svargam yānti triviṣṭapam
padaccheda.deva: येषाम् धर्मे न च स्पर्धा तेषाम् तत् ज्ञान-साधनम् ते ब्राह्मणाः इतः मुक्ताः स्वर्गम् यान्ति त्रिविष्टपम्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: Those who have no rivalry in dharma — for them that (action) is a means to knowledge. Those brāhmaṇas, freed from here, go to heaven, Triviṣṭapa (Brahman, which is full bliss).

notes: The edition prints tajjñānasādhanam as one word; Śaṅkara's gloss (tat yajñādikaṃ karma … jñānasādhanam) divides it as tat and jñānasādhanam.

Śaṅkara: those whose minds are not drawn by objects have no rivalry, no contention, over dharma such as the Jyotiṣṭoma, the means to transient fruit. For them, doing action for the Lord without regard to the fruit, that action, sacrifice and the rest, is the means to knowledge, through purification (as he says below: by merit destroying sin, he is then born lit by knowledge). Those brāhmaṇas who, pure in mind through sacrifice and the rest, know the Supreme Self as themselves, departing from this world of effect and cause, freed, go to svarga, which is happiness: Brahman, full bliss. Its difference from the other heaven is told by triviṣṭapa: it protects (pāti) one who has entered his own nature, freed from the three, the afflictions from oneself and the rest, or sattva and the rest, or waking and the rest; or it protects the qualified man who has entered (viṣṭa) it, (freed) by those three.

Śaṅkara, introducing the next verse: now he tells the conduct of the knower, the paramahaṃsa-parivrājaka-ācārya, who has renounced all actions from (the stage of) brahmacarya itself, has heard the Vedānta and the rest, and abides in his own glory.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्य सम्यक्समाचारमाहुर्वेदविदो जनाः ।
नैनं मन्येत भूयिष्ठं बाह्यमाभ्यन्तरं जनम् ॥ २७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasya samyaksamācāram āhur vedavido janāḥ |
nainaṃ manyeta bhūyiṣṭhaṃ bāhyam ābhyantaraṃ janam || 27 ||

lines.iast: tasya samyaksamācāram āhur vedavido janāḥ
nainaṃ manyeta bhūyiṣṭhaṃ bāhyam ābhyantaraṃ janam

padaccheda.iast: tasya samyak-samācāram āhuḥ veda-vidaḥ janāḥ na enam manyeta bhūyiṣṭham bāhyam ābhyantaram janam
padaccheda.deva: तस्य सम्यक्-समाचारम् आहुः वेद-विदः जनाः न एनम् मन्येत भूयिष्ठम् बाह्यम् आभ्यन्तरम् जनम्

translations.text: Those who know the Veda tell his right conduct: (he should live so that) people, outer and inner, do not think much of him.

notes: Śaṅkara: the knowers of the Veda tell the right conduct of that dispassionate knower: let (people) not think much of him, this yogin; people, inner and outer: the inner are sons, friends, wife and the like, the others the outer. That is, as sons, friends and the rest do not grasp him, so he lives beyond their range.
The construction is loose: Śaṅkara takes janam, though accusative, as those who are not to think much of the knower.

sanskrit.deva:
यत्र मन्येत भूयिष्ठं प्रावृषीव तृणोदकम् ।
अन्नपानं च ब्राह्मणस्तज्जीवेन्नानुसंज्वरेत् ॥ २८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yatra manyeta bhūyiṣṭhaṃ prāvṛṣīva tṛṇodakam |
annapānaṃ ca brāhmaṇas taj jīven nānusaṃjvaret || 28 ||

lines.iast: yatra manyeta bhūyiṣṭhaṃ prāvṛṣīva tṛṇodakam
annapānaṃ ca brāhmaṇas taj jīven nānusaṃjvaret

padaccheda.iast: yatra manyeta bhūyiṣṭham prāvṛṣi iva tṛṇa-udakam anna-pānam ca brāhmaṇaḥ tat jīvet na anusaṃjvaret
padaccheda.deva: यत्र मन्येत भूयिष्ठम् प्रावृषि इव तृण-उदकम् अन्न-पानम् च ब्राह्मणः तत् जीवेत् न अनुसंज्वरेत्

translations.text: Where the brāhmaṇa would find food and drink plentiful, as grass and water in the rains — (staying there) he should live on that, and not fret.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: in what kind of place does he live?

Śaṅkara: in a place free of trouble from wild beasts and the like, where he thinks food, drink and the rest are plentiful, as grass and water are plentiful in the rainy season. Some read tṛṇolapa, quoting ‘tṛṇolapa is known among the rice and other foods of munis’; others take it as a kind of sacred dūrvā grass. Staying there he should live on that food and drink, and not fret, not be troubled: otherwise, in a place without food and drink, he would be troubled how the life of the body could go on, and then there would be no success in yoga.

sanskrit.deva:
यत्राकथयमानस्य प्रयच्छत्यशिवं भयम् ।
अतिरिक्तमिवाकुर्वन्स श्रेयान्नेतरो जनः ॥ २९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yatrākathayamānasya prayacchaty aśivaṃ bhayam |
atiriktam ivākurvan sa śreyān netaro janaḥ || 29 ||

lines.iast: yatrākathayamānasya prayacchaty aśivaṃ bhayam
atiriktam ivākurvan sa śreyān netaro janaḥ

padaccheda.iast: yatra akathayamānasya prayacchati aśivam bhayam atiriktam iva akurvan saḥ śreyān na itaraḥ janaḥ
padaccheda.deva: यत्र अकथयमानस्य प्रयच्छति अशिवम् भयम् अतिरिक्तम् इव अकुर्वन् सः श्रेयान् न इतरः जनः

words.meaning: to one who does not speak (of himself)

translations.text: Where (a man) gives unkind fear (insult) to one who does not speak (of himself), not doing, as it were, anything more (than for any brāhmaṇa) — he is better (for the knower), not the other man.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: and (he should live) near people of this kind.

Śaṅkara: in the place where a man gives unkind fear, insult and the like, to the paramahaṃsa-parivrājaka-ācārya who does not speak, who is silent, hiding his greatness, clothed by anything, fed by anything, sleeping anywhere, seeing only the Self as the world, moving like one dull, dumb, a child or a goblin; ‘not doing anything more’: as one who knows the marks of the man of firm wisdom, knowing him to be a knower of Brahman, worships him as the Lord with prostration, salutation and the like — not doing, from not knowing him, more than the honour due to mere birth as a brāhmaṇa, the worship fitting a knower of Brahman, but rather insulting him: that man is better for this knower, not the other who worships him as the Lord with prostration and the rest (Manu 2.162: a learned brāhmaṇa should shrink from honour as from poison and always long for dishonour as for nectar; Parāśara: honour does the greatest harm to the wealth of yoga; the yogin despised by men gains success in yoga).

sanskrit.deva:
यो वाकथयमानस्य ह्यात्मानं नानुसंज्वरेत् ।
ब्रह्मस्वं नोपहन्याद्वा तदन्नं संमतं सताम् ॥ ३० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yo vākathayamānasya hy ātmānaṃ nānusaṃjvaret |
brahmasvaṃ nopahanyād vā tad annaṃ saṃmataṃ satām || 30 ||

lines.iast: yo vākathayamānasya hy ātmānaṃ nānusaṃjvaret
brahmasvaṃ nopahanyād vā tad annaṃ saṃmataṃ satām

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ vā akathayamānasya hi ātmānam na anusaṃjvaret brahma-svam na upahanyāt vā tat annam saṃmatam satām
padaccheda.deva: यः वा अकथयमानस्य हि आत्मानम् न अनुसंज्वरेत् ब्रह्म-स्वम् न उपहन्यात् वा तत् अन्नम् संमतम् सताम्

words.meaning: of one who does not speak (of himself)

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: He who does not vex the self of one who does not speak (of himself), or does not harm a brāhmaṇa's property — his food is approved by the good.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: whose food, then, is to be eaten?

Śaṅkara: he who does not vex the self of the one who does not speak, who is silent, who, having withdrawn all, abides as full bliss; or does not harm his brahmasva, the cloth, skin, kuśa grass, books and the like that are the means of his steadfastness in Brahman (‘jewels, gold and the like are not called the yogin's own; kuśa, bark, cloth and the like they know as the yogin's brahmasva’), or any other property of a brāhmaṇa: his food is approved by the good as fit to eat.

sanskrit.deva:
नित्यमज्ञातचर्या म इति मन्येत ब्राह्मणः ।
ज्ञातीनां तु वसन्मध्ये नैव विन्देत किंचन ॥ ३१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nityam ajñātacaryā ma iti manyeta brāhmaṇaḥ |
jñātīnāṃ tu vasan madhye naiva vindeta kiṃcana || 31 ||

lines.iast: nityam ajñātacaryā ma iti manyeta brāhmaṇaḥ
jñātīnāṃ tu vasan madhye naiva vindeta kiṃcana
lines.deva: ज्ञातीनां तु वसन्मध्ये नैव विन्देत किंचन

padaccheda.iast: nityam ajñāta-caryā me iti manyeta brāhmaṇaḥ jñātīnām tu vasan madhye na eva vindeta kiṃcana
padaccheda.deva: नित्यम् अज्ञात-चर्या मे इति मन्येत ब्राह्मणः ज्ञातीनाम् तु वसन् मध्ये न एव विन्देत किंचन

translations.text: ‘An unknown way of life is always to be mine’: so the brāhmaṇa should think. Living in the midst of kinsmen, he should take nothing at all (to himself).

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: again he tells the conduct of that same (knower).

Śaṅkara: nityam: without fail. ‘An unknown way of life, a hidden way of life, is to be mine’: so should the brāhmaṇa, the knower of Brahman, think. Living near kinsmen, sons, friends, wife and the like, he should not take, not accept, anything at all (some read kaścana). The yogin should not take up sons, friends, wife and the rest; abandoning them, devoted to his own Self alone, he should live hidden (a śruti: giving up family, sons and wife, the Vedāṅgas, sacrifice and the sacred thread, the muni should move hidden; Vasiṣṭha: he of whom no one knows whether he is good or not, learned or unlearned, of good or bad conduct, is a brāhmaṇa; though knowing, the wise man should act in the world like one dull). Liberation, the gaining of steadfastness in knowledge, is for such a man only, not for another, because of the many distractions.

Śaṅkara, second explanation: ajñātacaryā me: in the unknown — Brahman, not an object of the eye and the rest, beyond the reach of speech, abiding as knowledge that neither rises nor sets, untouched by hunger and the rest, whose nature is full bliss, within all, inward — conduct, steadfastness in the form of absorption (samādhi), is to be mine; not in the outward body, senses, sons, friends, wife and the rest, as ‘I am stout, I am lean, I go, I stand, impotent, one-eyed, dumb, deaf, the son of so-and-so, the grandson of this one, I am a brāhmaṇa, a kṣatriya, my wife, my son, my wealth, my dear kin and friends’: so should the brāhmaṇa, the knower of Brahman, think (Kena 1: what one does not see with the eye, but by which the eyes see, that alone is Brahman). Since steadfastness must be in the unknown Brahman, the kinsmen are the senses and the rest (a verse: anger, pride and the other faults, the objects and the senses, these are called the kinsmen of the embodied one); living among them — seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, going, eating, thinking, knowing — he should not take the Self to be the knower and the rest, for the Self is their witness (Chāndogya 8.12.4: he who knows ‘let me smell this’ is the Self). That is, he should not take the two bodies and their properties as the Self.
The edition: ma iti stands for me iti (the transcript marks the print's ‘ma’ as lacking the vowel-sign; the sandhi gives ma iti in any case); Śaṅkara glosses me, mama.

sanskrit.deva:
को ह्येवमन्तरात्मानं ब्राह्मणो मन्तुमर्हति ।
निर्लिङ्गमचलं शुद्धं सर्वद्वन्द्वविवर्जितम् ॥ ३२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ko hy evam antarātmānaṃ brāhmaṇo mantum arhati |
nirliṅgam acalaṃ śuddhaṃ sarvadvandvavivarjitam || 32 ||

lines.iast: ko hy evam antarātmānaṃ brāhmaṇo mantum arhati
nirliṅgam acalaṃ śuddhaṃ sarvadvandvavivarjitam

padaccheda.iast: kaḥ hi evam antarātmānam brāhmaṇaḥ mantum arhati nirliṅgam acalam śuddham sarva-dvandva-vivarjitam
padaccheda.deva: कः हि एवम् अन्तरात्मानम् ब्राह्मणः मन्तुम् अर्हति निर्लिङ्गम् अचलम् शुद्धम् सर्व-द्वन्द्व-विवर्जितम्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. acc. sg.

words.meaning: free of all pairs of opposites

translations.text: For what brāhmaṇa ought to think thus (as the body and its ways) of the inner Self, without marks, unmoving, pure, free of all pairs of opposites?

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: why is (the Self) not to be taken so?

Śaṅkara: nirliṅgam: free of the gross and the subtle (bodies); acalam: empty of action, agent and the rest; śuddham: free of the fault of ignorance; sarvadvandvavivarjitam: free of hunger, thirst, grief, delusion, old age, death, cold, heat, pleasure, pain and the other properties. What brāhmaṇa can think thus, in the way said, as the two bodies and their properties — ‘I am stout, I am lean, I go, I see, dumb, deaf, one-eyed, I am happy, I am unhappy’ — of the inner Self, within all, the witness of the knower and the rest, not an object of the means of knowledge? Were he to do so, his very being a brāhmaṇa would be lost (as he says below: he who does not depart from truth is to be known as a brāhmaṇa).

sanskrit.deva:
योऽन्यथा सन्तमात्मानमन्यथा प्रतिपद्यते ।
किं तेन न कृतं पापं चोरेणात्मापहारिणा ॥ ३३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yo 'nyathā santam ātmānam anyathā pratipadyate |
kiṃ tena na kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ coreṇātmāpahāriṇā || 33 ||

lines.iast: yo 'nyathā santam ātmānam anyathā pratipadyate
kiṃ tena na kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ coreṇātmāpahāriṇā
lines.deva: किं तेन न कृतं पापं चोरेणात्मापहारिणा

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ anyathā santam ātmānam anyathā pratipadyate kim tena na kṛtam pāpam coreṇa ātma-apahāriṇā
padaccheda.deva: यः अन्यथा सन्तम् आत्मानम् अन्यथा प्रतिपद्यते किम् तेन न कृतम् पापम् चोरेण आत्म-अपहारिणा

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: He who takes the Self, which is in one way, to be in another — what sin is not done by that thief, the stealer of the Self?

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: he who thinks so is the worst of sinners.

Śaṅkara: he who takes his Self, which is in one way — as knowledge, without marks, stainless, pure, free of all pairs, as Brahman, consciousness, being, bliss without a second — to be in another way, as the two bodies and their properties, ‘doer, enjoyer, happy, unhappy, I am stout, I am lean, the son of so-and-so, the grandson of this one, I am a brāhmaṇa, I am a kṣatriya’: what sin is not done by that fool who does not know the Self, the thief who steals the Self? All, the great sins and the rest, are done by him alone (Īśa 3: sunless are those worlds, covered by blind darkness; to them go after death those who slay the self; a verse: he who, having gained the state of a brāhmaṇa in this world, does not pass out of saṃsāra, is a slayer of Brahman). So, giving up taking as self the body, senses and the rest, which are objects, one should be steadfast in the Supreme Self, the unknown, beyond the reach of speech and the rest.

sanskrit.deva:
अश्रान्तः स्यादनादाता संमतो निरुपद्रवः ।
शिष्टो न शिष्टवत्स स्याद्ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मवित्कविः ॥ ३४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aśrāntaḥ syād anādātā saṃmato nirupadravaḥ |
śiṣṭo na śiṣṭavat sa syād brāhmaṇo brahmavit kaviḥ || 34 ||

lines.iast: aśrāntaḥ syād anādātā saṃmato nirupadravaḥ
śiṣṭo na śiṣṭavat sa syād brāhmaṇo brahmavit kaviḥ

padaccheda.iast: aśrāntaḥ syāt anādātā saṃmataḥ nirupadravaḥ śiṣṭaḥ na śiṣṭavat saḥ syāt brāhmaṇaḥ brahma-vit kaviḥ
padaccheda.deva: अश्रान्तः स्यात् अनादाता संमतः निरुपद्रवः शिष्टः न शिष्टवत् सः स्यात् ब्राह्मणः ब्रह्म-वित् कविः

words.meaning: one who does not take (to himself)

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: He who does not take (the not-self to himself) would be unwearied (by saṃsāra), esteemed, free from troubles. Though cultured, he should not be like a cultured man — that brāhmaṇa, the knower of Brahman, the sage.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: what comes to one who does not see the body, the senses and their properties (as self)?

Śaṅkara: anādātā: he who does not take up the not-self, the body, the senses and their properties, as self; that man is unwearied, not tired by saṃsāra, since hunger and the rest belong to the body and the rest (a śruti: hunger and thirst belong to prāṇa, grief and delusion to the mind, old age and death to the body); for when the two bodies are superimposed (on the Self), their properties are superimposed too. So, being unwearied, he is nirupadrava: the troubles are the obstacles, anger, joy, greed, delusion and the rest, and he is without them. saṃmataḥ: esteemed as cultured by the wise. He should not be like a cultured man, not behave so, but move like one dull: the brāhmaṇa, the knower of Brahman, the sage.

sanskrit.deva:
ये यथा वान्तमश्नन्ति बाला नित्यमभूतये ।
एवं ते वान्तमश्नन्ति स्ववीर्यस्योपभोजनात् ॥ ३५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ye yathā vāntam aśnanti bālā nityam abhūtaye |
evaṃ te vāntam aśnanti svavīryasyopabhojanāt || 35 ||

lines.iast: ye yathā vāntam aśnanti bālā nityam abhūtaye
evaṃ te vāntam aśnanti svavīryasyopabhojanāt

padaccheda.iast: ye yathā vāntam aśnanti bālāḥ nityam abhūtaye evam te vāntam aśnanti sva-vīryasya upabhojanāt
padaccheda.deva: ये यथा वान्तम् अश्नन्ति बालाः नित्यम् अभूतये एवम् ते वान्तम् अश्नन्ति स्व-वीर्यस्य उपभोजनात्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. acc. sg.
past passive participle n. acc. sg.

translations.text: As children (dogs and fools) eat vomit, always to their ruin, so those (who make their greatness known) eat vomit, by making use of their own power.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: now, censuring the one who does not move hidden, he says this.

Śaṅkara: bāla is used of a fool and of a dog (‘the fool is called bāla, the dog too is known as bāla’). As children, dogs or fools eat vomit, what has been thrown up, so those cultured knowers of Brahman who proclaim their own greatness and do not move hidden eat vomit, because they make use of their own power; this eating of vomit is to their ruin, for evil only. So he should be hidden and behave as one not cultured.

sanskrit.deva:
अनाढ्या मानुषे वित्ते आढ्या वेदेषु ये द्विजाः ।
ते दुर्धर्षा दुष्प्रकम्प्या विद्यात्तान्ब्रह्मणस्तनुम् ॥ ३६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
anāḍhyā mānuṣe vitte āḍhyā vedeṣu ye dvijāḥ |
te durdharṣā duṣprakampyā vidyāt tān brahmaṇas tanum || 36 ||

lines.iast: anāḍhyā mānuṣe vitte āḍhyā vedeṣu ye dvijāḥ
lines.deva: अनाढ्या मानुषे वित्ते आढ्या वेदेषु ये द्विजाः

lines.iast: te durdharṣā duṣprakampyā vidyāt tān brahmaṇas tanum

padaccheda.iast: anāḍhyāḥ mānuṣe vitte āḍhyāḥ vedeṣu ye dvijāḥ te durdharṣāḥ duṣprakampyāḥ vidyāt tān brahmaṇaḥ tanum
padaccheda.deva: अनाढ्याः मानुषे वित्ते आढ्याः वेदेषु ये द्विजाः ते दुर्धर्षाः दुष्प्रकम्प्याः विद्यात् तान् ब्रह्मणः तनुम्

translations.text: The twice-born who are not rich in human wealth, (but) rich in the Vedas — they are unassailable, not to be shaken; one should know them as the body of Brahman.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: now, praising the yogin, he says this.

Śaṅkara: anāḍhyāḥ: not esteemed, unattached in mind, in human wealth, wife, sons, riches and the like; rich in the Vedas: in what the Vedas teach, non-violence, truth, not stealing, non-possession, brahmacarya and the means to absorption (samādhi). Those twice-born are unassailable, not to be shaken; one should know them as the body of Brahman, of the very nature of Brahman.

sanskrit.deva:
सर्वान्स्विष्टकृतो देवान्विद्याद्य इह कश्चन ।
न समानो ब्राह्मणस्य यस्मिन्प्रयतते स्वयम् ॥ ३७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sarvān sviṣṭakṛto devān vidyād ya iha kaścana |
na samāno brāhmaṇasya yasmin prayatate svayam || 37 ||

lines.iast: sarvān sviṣṭakṛto devān vidyād ya iha kaścana
na samāno brāhmaṇasya yasmin prayatate svayam

padaccheda.iast: sarvān sviṣṭakṛtaḥ devān vidyāt yaḥ iha kaścana na samānaḥ brāhmaṇasya yasmin prayatate svayam
padaccheda.deva: सर्वान् स्विष्टकृतः देवान् विद्यात् यः इह कश्चन न समानः ब्राह्मणस्य यस्मिन् प्रयतते स्वयम्

translations.text: Whoever here would know all the gods who make the offering well (and sacrifice to them) is not equal to the brāhmaṇa (who knows Brahman); nor is (the god) toward whom he himself strives (with his offering).

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: further, this is the greatness of the knower of Brahman.

Śaṅkara: sarvān: Agni and the rest; sviṣṭakṛtaḥ: those who make (the offering) well offered (a śruti: making it well offered, he is Sviṣṭakṛt). Whoever here would know the gods, each one, for the giving (of the oblation), even one who sacrifices to all the deities, is not equal to the brāhmaṇa, the knower of Brahman. Nor is this a wonder: even the particular deity toward which the sacrificer himself strives for the fruit, giving the oblation with ‘this to Agni, this to Indra’, the deity that is the counterpart of the oblation, is not equal to the knower of Brahman; how much less the sacrificer, a beast of the gods (the Mokṣadharma: even (the god) to whom the best of the twice-born sacrifices with the mantra does not come near the likeness of the brāhmaṇa, how much less (the sacrificer); Manu: there is no being here higher than the knowers of Brahman).

sanskrit.deva:
यमप्रयतमानं तु मानयन्ति स मानितः ।
न मान्यमानो मन्येत नावमाने विसंज्वरेत् ॥ ३८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yam aprayatamānaṃ tu mānayanti sa mānitaḥ |
na mānyamāno manyeta nāvamāne visaṃjvaret || 38 ||

lines.iast: yam aprayatamānaṃ tu mānayanti sa mānitaḥ
na mānyamāno manyeta nāvamāne visaṃjvaret

padaccheda.iast: yam aprayatamānam tu mānayanti saḥ mānitaḥ na mānyamānaḥ manyeta na avamāne visaṃjvaret
padaccheda.deva: यम् अप्रयतमानम् तु मानयन्ति सः मानितः न मान्यमानः मन्येत न अवमाने विसंज्वरेत्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: He who does not strive, whom (people) honour — honoured, he should not, while being honoured, think (of himself as honoured); in dishonour he should not be distressed.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: again he tells the conduct of that same (knower).

Śaṅkara: yam: the knower of Brahman who does not strive, who is silent, who, having withdrawn all, abides in his own glory, who has renounced from (the stage of) brahmacarya itself, whose meaning is fixed by the knowledge of the Vedānta, the paramahaṃsa-parivrājaka-ācārya who moves hidden. If some who are wise, knowing the marks of the man of firm wisdom, think ‘he is a knower of Brahman’ and honour him, worship him, then that knower, worshipped by them, should not think ‘I am honoured’. And if those who do not know the marks of the man of firm wisdom, thinking him dull, dishonour him, he should not on that account fret, should not be pained.
Śaṅkara, introducing verses 39 and 40: how then should the honoured or the dishonoured one think? He says it in two verses.

sanskrit.deva:
लोकस्वभाववृत्तिर्हि निमेषोन्मेषवत्सदा ।
विद्वांसो मानयन्तीह इति मन्येत मानितः ॥ ३९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
lokasvabhāvavṛttir hi nimeṣonmeṣavat sadā |
vidvāṃso mānayantīha iti manyeta mānitaḥ || 39 ||

lines.iast: lokasvabhāvavṛttir hi nimeṣonmeṣavat sadā
vidvāṃso mānayantīha iti manyeta mānitaḥ

padaccheda.iast: loka-svabhāva-vṛttiḥ hi nimeṣa-unmeṣa-vat sadā vidvāṃsaḥ mānayanti iha iti manyeta mānitaḥ
padaccheda.deva: लोक-स्वभाव-वृत्तिः हि निमेष-उन्मेष-वत् सदा विद्वांसः मानयन्ति इह इति मन्येत मानितः

words.meaning: the natural way of the world
like the closing and opening of the eyes

grammar.en: past active participle m. nom. pl.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: ‘That the wise honour (one) here is the natural way of the world, always, like the closing and opening of the eyes’: so the honoured one should think.

notes: Śaṅkara comments on verses 39 and 40 together.
Śaṅkara: that the wise honour the knower of Brahman is their natural activity, like the closing and opening of the eyes: so the honoured one should think.

words.meaning: without (knowledge of) the world and the śāstras

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: ‘Those who do not know dharma, deluded, without (the knowledge of) the world and the śāstras, will not honour one worthy of honour’: so the one not honoured should think.

notes: Śaṅkara: likewise, dishonoured, despised by people, the knower should think thus: the deluded, without discernment, without the world and the śāstras, will not honour one worthy of honour; they will not honour even the honourable: this is the nature of the ignorant. So the one not honoured, not worshipped, should think.

adharmaviduṣaḥ, which Śaṅkara does not gloss, is taken here as a- with dharmaviduṣaḥ, ‘not knowing dharma’, with the form of the accusative used for the nominative; it could also be read ‘knowing adharma’.

translations.text: Honour and silence never dwell together; for this (world) is the field of honour, that (other) of silence: they know it as ‘That’.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: now he tells that honour and silence have different fields.

Śaṅkara: honour and silence never dwell together, in one place. This world, the manifold that is the range of perception and the other means of knowledge, called loka because it is seen (lokyate), is the field of honour. That other world is the field of silence; which is it? They know it as ‘tat’: ‘tat’ is a name of Brahman (Gītā 17.23: Om tat sat is held to be the threefold designation of Brahman; the Anugītā: ‘Om tat sat’ and ‘to Viṣṇu’ grant union and the rest). Brahman, denoted by the word ‘tat’, is the field of silence. That is: by honour one reaches saṃsāra, by silence Brahman (the Hairaṇyagarbha: the inclination toward enjoyments, food, women and the like, is called honour; silence is called the cause of gaining the happiness of the bliss of Brahman).
In the print (p. 232) the gloss runs asau paraloko maunasya ko 'sau tat viduḥ without a stop; it is read as a question and its answer.

words.meaning: from dwelling among the things of honour

translations.text: Fortune (comes) from dwelling among the things of honour, and that (fortune) is an obstacle; the fortune of Brahman is very hard to gain for one lacking wisdom, O warrior.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: now he shows that for one who dwells among the things of honour there is no liberation.

Śaṅkara: from dwelling in the field of honour: for one who moves in the manifold that is the range of honour and performs the action that is the means to heaven, cattle, food and the like, blinded by the poison of objects, there is fortune. And that fortune is an obstacle, opposed to the path of the highest good (the Mokṣadharma: the delight of one dwelling in the village is a binding rope; cutting it the good go on, the evil do not cut it). By one so overcome by fortune, deluded, engaged in objects, lacking wisdom, lacking knowledge, the fortune of Brahman, which is the bliss of Brahman, is very hard to gain (the Hairaṇyagarbha: that which is eternal, a mass of consciousness and bliss, free of guṇa and form, called bliss, supreme, pure, is called the fortune of Brahman). It cannot even be heard of (Kaṭha 1.2.7: he whom many cannot even hear of).

translations.text: The good rightly declare the doors (to the fortune of Brahman), of many kinds, hard to practise: truth and uprightness, modesty, restraint, purity and knowledge — six, which bar honour and delusion.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: now he shows the doors by which one enters the fortune of Brahman.

Śaṅkara: the doors are the doors for entering the fortune of Brahman; the good declare them rightly; of many kinds, hard to practise. Which are they? satya: speaking of things as they are, and the good of beings; ārjava: freedom from crookedness; hrī: shame at doing what should not be done; dama: the quieting of the inner organ (some say: of the outer organs); śauca: the washing away of impurity; vidyā: the knowledge of Brahman. These six bar honour and delusion.
